verses.1: Listen, children, to a father's discipline and give attention to know understanding.
verses.2: For I have given you a good instruction; do not abandon my teaching.
verses.3: I was a son to my father, tender, and a beloved only child to my mother.
verses.4: He taught me and said to me: Let your heart hold fast to my words; keep my commandments and live.
verses.5: Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding; do not forget, and do not turn away from the words of my mouth.
verses.6: Do not abandon her, and she will guard you; love her, and she will keep you.
verses.7: The beginning of wisdom is to acquire wisdom; with all your acquiring, acquire understanding.
verses.8: Cherish her, and she will exalt you; honor her, and she will give you honor.
verses.9: She will place a wreath of grace on your head; she will give you a crown of splendor as a shield.
verses.10: Listen, my son, and take my words; let many years of life be added to you.
verses.11: I have taught you the way of wisdom; I have guided you in the paths of uprightness.
verses.12: When you walk, your steps will not falter; when you run, you will not stumble.
verses.13: Hold fast to discipline; do not let it slip from you. Guard it, for it is your life.
verses.14: Do not enter the path of the wicked, and do not walk in the way of the evil.
verses.15: Avoid it; do not pass by it. Turn away from it and go on.
verses.16: For they will not sleep unless they do harm; their sleep is taken away unless they cause someone to stumble.
verses.17: For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.
verses.18: But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until the day is fully come.
verses.19: The way of the wicked is like darkness; they do not know what causes them to stumble.
verses.20: My son, give attention to my words; incline your ear to my sayings.
verses.21: Let them not escape from your eyes; keep them within your heart.
verses.22: For they are life to those who find them, and healing for all flesh.
verses.23: Above all else, guard your heart, for from it come the sources of life.
verses.24: Put away crooked speech from yourself; keep deceitful words far from you.
verses.25: Let your eyes look directly forward; let your gaze be fixed before you.
verses.26: Make level the paths for your feet, and all your ways will be established.
verses.27: Do not turn to the right or to the left; remove your foot from evil.

notes:
Notes
- v. 17: "the bread of wickedness" and "the wine of violence" reflect metaphorical language, aligning with the context of moral corruption.
- v. 23: "Above all else" translates the Hebrew "מִכָּל" (mikol) in context, emphasizing the primacy of guarding the heart.
- v. 27: The final verse uses "remove your foot from evil" to mirror the parallel imperative and convey the idea of avoiding wrongdoing.
